description: Limits describe function behavior near a point and underpin all of calculus.
common_misconceptions: Treats limit value as always equal to function value at that point

description: Read approximate limit values by tracing y values as x approaches a target from a graph.
common_misconceptions: Reads the open circle value instead of the nearby trend
Ignores one-sided approach direction

description: Use input output tables with x values closer to a target to estimate a limit numerically.
common_misconceptions: Assumes the last table entry is the exact limit
Uses values far from the target point

description: Evaluate left hand and right hand limits to describe approach from a single direction.
common_misconceptions: Assumes left and right limits are always equal
Mixes up notation for x approaches a from left vs right

description: Apply sum, difference, product, quotient, and constant multiple rules to evaluate limits of combinations.
common_misconceptions: Applies quotient law when denominator limit is zero
Distributes limits incorrectly across products

description: Factor, rationalize, or simplify expressions to resolve indeterminate forms before taking a limit.
common_misconceptions: Cancels terms that are not common factors
Stops simplifying before the indeterminate form is removed

description: Select graph, table, or algebraic methods based on how the function is presented.
common_misconceptions: Forces algebra when a graph already shows the limit
Uses tables when exact algebra is straightforward

description: Bound a function between two others with the same limit to prove the middle function shares that limit.
common_misconceptions: Fails to verify inequalities hold near the target point
Uses bounds that do not share the same limit

description: Relate graphical, numerical, and analytical limit information for the same function.
common_misconceptions: Treats representations as unrelated answers
Ignores mismatch signals between graph and algebra

description: Describe end behavior and unbounded growth using limits as x approaches positive or negative infinity.
common_misconceptions: Confuses infinity as a number with unbounded behavior
Swaps signs for x approaches negative infinity

description: Identify horizontal asymptotes using limits of a function as x approaches plus or minus infinity.
common_misconceptions: Equates horizontal asymptote with any horizontal line the graph crosses
Finds only one side of end behavior

description: Locate vertical asymptotes where function values grow without bound as x approaches a finite value.
common_misconceptions: Marks a hole as a vertical asymptote
Assumes infinite limit implies the function equals infinity

description: A function is continuous at a point when the limit, function value, and approach all agree.
common_misconceptions: Checks only that f(a) exists
Ignores whether the limit equals f(a)

description: Classify removable, jump, and infinite discontinuities from limits and graph features.
common_misconceptions: Labels every gap as removable
Confuses jump discontinuity with infinite discontinuity

description: Determine whether a function is continuous on open or closed intervals using endpoint rules.
common_misconceptions: Requires differentiability for continuity on an interval
Ignores endpoint one sided limits on closed intervals

description: Use IVT on continuous functions to guarantee a target value is hit between two inputs.
common_misconceptions: Applies IVT without checking continuity on the interval
Assumes IVT gives the exact x location

description: Define a new function value at a removable discontinuity so the limit matches the assigned value.
common_misconceptions: Redefines values at jump discontinuities expecting continuity
Forgets to state the single corrected value

description: Compute average rate of change as the slope of a secant line over an interval.
common_misconceptions: Uses a single point instead of two endpoints
Confuses average rate with instantaneous rate

description: Instantaneous rate is the limit of average rates as the interval shrinks around a point.
common_misconceptions: Treats instantaneous rate as average over a tiny but nonzero interval only
Assumes instantaneous rate exists everywhere

description: A tangent line matches local direction; secant lines connect two points on a curve.
common_misconceptions: Draws tangent using two distant points only
Equates secant slope with tangent slope without a limit

node_name: Definition of the derivative as a limit
description: The derivative at a is the limit of the difference quotient as h approaches zero.
common_misconceptions: Substitutes h equals zero before simplifying
Uses the wrong difference quotient form

description: Estimate f prime at a point from the tangent slope or nearby secant slopes on a graph.
common_misconceptions: Reads derivative sign from y value instead of slope
Uses a secant through unrelated points

description: Differentiability implies continuity, but continuity does not guarantee a derivative exists.
common_misconceptions: Assumes continuous functions are always differentiable
Thinks a sharp corner is differentiable

description: Differentiate x raised to n by bringing down the exponent and reducing the power by one.
common_misconceptions: Forgets to subtract one from the exponent
Applies power rule to exponential functions like 2 to the x

description: The derivative of a sum or difference is the sum or difference of the derivatives.
common_misconceptions: Differentiates only one term in a sum
Applies product rule to simple sums

description: A constant factor stays outside when differentiating a function multiple.
common_misconceptions: Differentiates the constant into a nonzero term incorrectly
Drops the constant factor entirely

description: The derivative of any constant function is zero everywhere.
common_misconceptions: Writes the constant as the derivative
Treats constants as variable terms

node_name: Derivatives of sin x and cos x
description: Memorize and apply that sine differentiates to cosine and cosine differentiates to negative sine.
common_misconceptions: Differentiates sin to negative cos
Swaps sin and cos derivative signs

node_name: Derivative of e to the x
description: The exponential e to the x equals its own derivative for all real x.
common_misconceptions: Treats e to the x like a power function
Introduces a coefficient of ln e incorrectly

description: The derivative of natural log x is one over x for positive x.
common_misconceptions: Uses one over x for ln of any expression without chain rule
Differentiates ln x as ln

node_name: Derivative notation f prime and dy dx
description: Translate between f prime of x, dy dx, and operator notation for the same derivative.
common_misconceptions: Treats dy and dx as separate unrelated numbers always
Confuses f prime with f itself

description: Differentiate repeatedly to obtain second and higher derivatives when they exist.
common_misconceptions: Stops after first derivative for concavity questions
Assumes second derivative always exists

description: If position is s of t, velocity is s prime of t and acceleration is the next derivative.
common_misconceptions: Uses position as velocity
Confuses speed with signed velocity

description: Differentiate a composite function by multiplying outer and inner derivatives.
common_misconceptions: Forgets to multiply by the inner derivative
Confuses chain rule with product rule

description: Identify inner and outer layers in nested functions before applying the chain rule.
common_misconceptions: Treats nested functions as a product
Differentiates only the outer layer

description: Differentiate both sides of an equation with respect to x and collect dy dx terms.
common_misconceptions: Forgets to differentiate y terms with chain rule
Drops dy dx factor when differentiating y

description: Apply implicit differentiation to relations with products, quotients, or trig inside y terms.
common_misconceptions: Applies explicit rules only to y terms
Fails to isolate dy dx after differentiation

description: Use g prime of y equals one over f prime of g of y when f and g are inverses.
common_misconceptions: Reciprocates the function value instead of the derivative
Uses wrong variable when evaluating f prime

description: Differentiate inverse sine with the one over square root of one minus x squared form on its domain.
common_misconceptions: Omits absolute value considerations in general forms
Confuses with inverse cos derivative sign

description: Differentiate inverse cosine with the negative one over square root of one minus x squared form.
common_misconceptions: Uses the same sign as inverse sine
Forgets domain restrictions near endpoints

description: Differentiate inverse tangent as one over one plus x squared.
common_misconceptions: Uses reciprocal tangent formula incorrectly
Mixes inverse tan with inverse sin forms

description: Take natural log of both sides to simplify products, quotients, or variable exponents before differentiating.
common_misconceptions: Logs only one factor of a product
Forgets implicit step after logging

node_name: Differentiating general exponential a to the x
description: Differentiate a to the x using a to the x times ln a when a is a positive constant.
common_misconceptions: Applies power rule to a to the x
Uses ln a in the exponent instead of as a factor

description: Choose among power, product, quotient, chain, and implicit methods based on function structure.
common_misconceptions: Defaults to product rule for every composite
Uses quotient rule when chain rule suffices

description: Differentiate component functions with respect to a parameter when motion is given parametrically.
common_misconceptions: Differentiates with respect to x when t is the parameter
Ignores chain relationship between t and x

description: Connect position, velocity, and acceleration functions in motion problems using derivatives.
common_misconceptions: Integrates when differentiation is required
Uses speed when direction matters

description: Draw a diagram, label variables, and relate their rates with an equation before differentiating.
common_misconceptions: Differentiates before writing a relating equation
Treats all rates as constants incorrectly

description: Use geometric formulas such as Pythagorean theorem or similar triangles in related rates.
common_misconceptions: Uses outdated geometry after dimensions change
Forgets to differentiate constants properly

description: Relate trigonometric angle variables to lengths and differentiate with respect to time.
common_misconceptions: Forgets chain rule on angle functions of time
Uses degrees without converting when needed

description: Approximate a function near a point using the tangent line value at that point.
common_misconceptions: Uses secant line far from the point
Confuses linearization with tangent line equation always at zero

description: Evaluate L of x equals f of a plus f prime of a times x minus a for nearby estimates.
common_misconceptions: Uses wrong anchor point a
Omits f prime of a factor on x minus a

description: Relate dy equals f prime of x dx as a local change estimate along the tangent.
common_misconceptions: Treats dy and dx as always equal to actual delta y and delta x
Uses differentials far from the linearization point

node_name: L Hopital rule indeterminate zero over zero
description: Differentiate numerator and denominator separately when a limit yields zero over zero locally.
common_misconceptions: Applies L Hopital without verifying indeterminate form
Differentiates only one side of the fraction once incorrectly

node_name: L Hopital rule indeterminate infinity over infinity
description: Apply L Hopital when limits produce infinity over infinity and other conditions are met.
common_misconceptions: Uses L Hopital on infinity minus infinity without rewrite
Assumes one application always finishes the limit

description: Analyze when a particle speeds up, slows down, or changes direction using velocity and acceleration signs.
common_misconceptions: Equates positive velocity with speeding up always
Ignores acceleration opposite to velocity

node_name: Rates of change in applied contexts
description: Interpret derivatives as marginal or instantaneous rates in science and economics style settings.
common_misconceptions: Reports units without per input variable
Uses average rate where instantaneous is asked

description: Recognize that tangent estimates are most accurate very close to the linearization point.
common_misconceptions: Expects zero error everywhere on the tangent
Uses linearization far outside a small neighborhood

description: On a continuous interval, some point has instantaneous rate equal to the average rate over the interval.
common_misconceptions: Applies MVT without continuity on the closed interval
Confuses average rate with function average value

description: Continuous functions on closed intervals attain absolute maximum and minimum values.
common_misconceptions: Assumes extrema occur only at endpoints
Ignores interior critical points

description: Find points where f prime is zero or undefined to locate candidate extrema.
common_misconceptions: Assumes every critical point is an extremum
Forgets to check where derivative is undefined

description: Use sign changes of f prime around critical points to classify local maxima and minima.
common_misconceptions: Classifies without checking sign on both sides
Treats zero derivative alone as proof of max

description: f increases where f prime is positive and decreases where f prime is negative.
common_misconceptions: Uses f sign instead of f prime sign
Ignores undefined derivative intervals

description: Compare critical values and endpoint values to find absolute max and min on a closed interval.
common_misconceptions: Checks only critical points
Compares only relative extrema

description: f is concave up where f double prime is positive and concave down where f double prime is negative.
common_misconceptions: Uses first derivative sign for concavity
Assumes concavity matches increase decrease

description: Inflection points occur where concavity changes, often at zeros of f double prime with a sign change.
common_misconceptions: Labels any f double prime zero as inflection without sign change
Confuses inflection with critical points

description: If f prime is zero and f double prime is nonzero, the sign of f double prime classifies max or min.
common_misconceptions: Applies when f double prime is zero inconclusively without first derivative test
Uses at non critical points

description: Build a function sketch from sign charts of f prime and f double prime and key values.
common_misconceptions: Sketches without connecting to given f values
Ignores asymptotes when sketching

description: Define variables, constraints, and a single objective function to maximize or minimize.
common_misconceptions: Optimizes without a constraint relating variables
Uses wrong variable as the objective

description: Substitute constraint equations to express the objective in one variable before differentiating.
common_misconceptions: Differentiates before substitution
Forgets domain restrictions from context

description: Solve max min problems from area, volume, or distance geometry with feasible domains.
common_misconceptions: Accepts negative lengths or areas
Checks endpoints poorly on closed domains

node_name: Connecting f f prime and f double prime
description: Interpret how function, slope, and curvature graphs relate at the same x values.
common_misconceptions: Assumes f positive means f prime positive
Matches peaks of f with peaks of f prime always

description: List critical points and endpoints as candidates then compare function values for absolute extrema.
common_misconceptions: Omits endpoints on closed intervals
Compares derivatives instead of function values

description: Distinguish local peaks and valleys from the highest and lowest values on an entire domain.
common_misconceptions: Assumes local max is global max
Ignores domain boundaries for global extrema

description: An antiderivative F of f satisfies F prime equals f on an interval.
common_misconceptions: Forgets the constant of integration
Assumes antiderivative is unique without plus C

description: Write families of antiderivatives with integral notation and include plus C.
common_misconceptions: Omits plus C in indefinite integrals
Treats indefinite integral as a number

description: Reverse power, sum, and constant multiple rules to integrate polynomials and simple combinations.
common_misconceptions: Adds one to the exponent when integrating power terms incorrectly
Integrates sum term by term with missing C once only

node_name: Integrals of sin cos e to the x and one over x
description: Apply standard antiderivatives for trig and exponential forms including one over x as ln absolute x.
common_misconceptions: Integrates e to the x with power rule
Forgets absolute value in ln antiderivative discussions

node_name: Riemann sums left right and midpoint
description: Approximate definite integrals using left, right, and midpoint rectangle sums on partitions.
common_misconceptions: Uses wrong sample point for the chosen rule
Confuses number of rectangles with partition width

description: Average endpoint heights on subintervals to approximate area under a curve with trapezoids.
common_misconceptions: Uses rectangle rules when trapezoids are specified
Doubles interval width incorrectly

node_name: Definite integral as limit of Riemann sums
description: A definite integral is the limit of Riemann sums as partition norm goes to zero when it exists.
common_misconceptions: Treats finite Riemann sum as exact integral always
Uses unequal widths without weighting correctly

description: If F of x is integral from a to x of f of t dt, then F prime of x equals f of x for continuous f.
common_misconceptions: Differentiates with respect to the wrong limit
Forgets chain rule when upper limit is composite

description: Evaluate definite integrals using any antiderivative F with F of b minus F of a.
common_misconceptions: Subtracts in wrong order b minus a reversed
Uses indefinite integral without evaluating bounds

description: Find antiderivatives then apply FTC part 2, or use geometry when shapes are clear.
common_misconceptions: Leaves plus C in a definite evaluation incorrectly
Splits integrals without continuity justification

description: Interpret integrals with variable upper limits as accumulated change from a fixed start.
common_misconceptions: Treats variable limit as a constant
Confuses accumulated amount with rate

description: Integral of rate over time gives net change in the underlying quantity.
common_misconceptions: Uses rate at an endpoint instead of integrating
Confuses net change with total distance always

description: Choose u and du to rewrite an integral into a simpler form and back substitute.
common_misconceptions: Forgets to change dx to du completely
Fails to back substitute after integrating in u

description: Change both integrand and bounds when using u substitution on definite integrals.
common_misconceptions: Keeps original bounds after switching to u
Back substitutes then also changes bounds twice

description: Attach correct units and meaning to integral results in applied settings.
common_misconceptions: Reports rate units instead of accumulated units
Ignores sign meaning in context

description: Use linearity, interval additivity, and symmetry to simplify integral calculations.
common_misconceptions: Reverses bounds without sign change
Splits at discontinuities without separate limits

description: Translate verbal rates of change into equations involving derivatives of unknown functions.
common_misconceptions: Uses algebraic equations without derivatives
Swaps independent and dependent variables

description: Substitute a proposed function and its derivatives to confirm it satisfies the equation.
common_misconceptions: Checks only the original function without derivatives
Accepts solutions outside stated domain

description: Read short segment slopes on a grid to infer solution curve behavior without solving explicitly.
common_misconceptions: Draws curves ignoring segment slopes
Assumes all slope fields have explicit formulas

description: Compute dy dx at grid points and sketch consistent slope segments for a given differential equation.
common_misconceptions: Uses wrong ratio for dy dx at each point
Sketches segments with inconsistent scale

description: Match initial conditions to solution curves suggested by a slope field picture.
common_misconceptions: Ignores initial point when selecting a curve
Crosses segments perpendicular incorrectly often

description: Rewrite dy dx as g of y times h of x when variables can be isolated on separate sides.
common_misconceptions: Separates incorrectly when variables are entangled
Loses constant solutions during separation

description: Integrate both sides after separation and solve for the unknown function with initial data.
common_misconceptions: Integrates only one side
Forgets absolute value or domain restrictions in ln steps

description: Model proportional growth with dy dt equals k y and exponential solutions.
common_misconceptions: Uses linear growth instead of exponential
Chooses wrong sign for k in growth

description: Model proportional decay with negative rate constant and decreasing exponential solutions.
common_misconceptions: Uses growth formula with positive k for decay
Confuses half life with doubling time formula

description: Use an initial condition to determine the constant after finding a general solution.
common_misconceptions: Substitutes initial data before integrating
Uses wrong variable in the initial condition

description: The average value of f on a b is one over b minus a times the integral of f from a to b.
common_misconceptions: Averages endpoints only
Forgets to divide by interval length

node_name: Area between curves with vertical slices
description: Integrate top minus bottom function difference with respect to x on intersection bounds.
common_misconceptions: Integrates bottom minus top without absolute value awareness
Uses wrong intersection limits

node_name: Area between curves with horizontal slices
description: Integrate right minus left function difference with respect to y when slicing horizontally.
common_misconceptions: Keeps dx when integrating with respect to y
Swaps right and left functions

description: Revolve a region about an axis and integrate pi times radius squared for cross sectional disks.
common_misconceptions: Uses radius without squaring
Uses wrong axis distance as radius

description: Subtract inner disk area from outer disk area when a hole appears in the solid of revolution.
common_misconceptions: Subtracts radii before squaring
Uses washer when a solid disk suffices

description: Decide whether an inner radius is zero or positive before setting up the volume integral.
common_misconceptions: Always uses washer notation
Ignores gap between region and axis of rotation

description: Integrate cross sectional area functions perpendicular to an axis when shapes are given.
common_misconceptions: Uses disk formula when cross sections are not circles
Forgets to express area in one variable

description: Integrate velocity over time to find net displacement of a particle.
common_misconceptions: Uses speed integral for displacement
Confuses displacement with total distance

description: Integrate absolute value of velocity or split intervals by sign to find total path length.
common_misconceptions: Uses displacement integral for total distance
Forgets to split where velocity changes sign

description: Interpret definite integrals of density or rate functions as totals over an interval.
common_misconceptions: Reports average when total is requested
Uses wrong units after integration

description: Recover position from velocity or velocity from acceleration using initial conditions and integrals.
common_misconceptions: Omits plus C before applying initial data
Differentiates when integration is needed

description: Draw the region and axis, identify a representative slice, and express radius or area correctly.
common_misconceptions: Labels radius from wrong reference line
Uses inconsistent variable of integration

description: Explain what a computed integral represents including units in applied volume and motion problems.
common_misconceptions: Gives numeric answer without context
Multiplies units incorrectly

description: Split integrals at breakpoints where formulas or behavior change on the interval of integration.
common_misconceptions: Integrates across a jump without splitting
Uses wrong formula on a subinterval
